tasks.title: Force-push rule reads git configuration values
tasks.summary: The force-push rule reads a command named in a git configuration value (-c, --config-env, GIT_CONFIG_*, GIT_PAGER, GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, -O) the same way it reads the in-line form.
tasks.objective: Make `checkForcePush` in factory/orchestrator/src/policy.ts read a command line carried by a git configuration value the same way it reads that command line typed directly. Today an inline `alias.` definition is refused by `definesInlineGitAlias`; extend the same reading to every configuration value that git runs as a command: a `-c key=value` or `--config-env=key=VAR` on the git command, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` / `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>`, `GIT_PAGER`, `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF`, and the `-O<cmd>` / `--open-files-in-pager=<cmd>` option of `git grep`. Each value is read whether it is set on the git command itself, in an earlier `export` or assignment segment of the same command line, or through `env`. A readable value is dequoted and checked by the same force-push checks a `sh -c` payload goes through; a value the rule cannot read statically is refused the way an unreadable inline alias is, whatever its key.
acceptance_criteria: Each of these is refused with the force-push violation: `git -c core.pager='git push --force origin main' log`; `git -c diff.external='git push -f origin main' diff`; `GIT_PAGER='git push -f origin main' git log`; `env GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF='git push --force origin main' git diff`; `export GIT_PAGER='git push -f origin main'; git log`; `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.pager GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0='git push -f origin main' git log`; `git grep -O'git push -f origin main' x`; `git grep --open-files-in-pager='git push --force origin main' x`.

A configuration value the rule cannot read statically is refused, whatever its key: `git -c core.pager="$P" log`, `git -c user.name="$NAME" commit -m y`, `export GIT_PAGER="$P"; git log`, `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF=$(cat f) git diff`, a backtick value, and `git --config-env=core.pager=SOMEVAR log`.

Each of these is still allowed: `git -c color.ui=always log`, `git -c core.pager=cat log`, `GIT_PAGER=cat git log`, `env GIT_PAGER=less git log`, `git -c user.name=x commit -m y`, `git log --oneline`, `git grep -n foo`.

`GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` is read entry by entry, each entry by the same rule as a `-c key=value`, in both entry spellings git writes: the single-quoted `'key=value'` and the `'key'='value'` form that git 2.31 and later writes, with several entries in one value separated by spaces and the two spellings mixed. Each case is its own named test in policyGitConfig.test.ts: `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'core.pager=git push -f origin main'" git log` and `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'core.pager'='git push -f origin main'" git log` are each refused with the force-push violation; `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'color.ui=always'" git log` and `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'color.ui'='always'" git log` are each allowed; `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'color.ui'='always' 'core.pager=git push --force origin main'" git log`, a two-entry value in which only the second entry changes what git runs, is refused with the force-push violation; `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="$X" git log` is refused as unreadable.
Every existing test in factory/orchestrator/test/policy.test.ts and policyHookEntry.test.ts passes unchanged.
Each new branch of the rule is proven by mutation: the result names, per branch, the test that fails when that branch is disabled.

The rule reads every value of every carrier the objective names and needs no list of configuration keys: an unreadable value is refused whatever its key, and a readable value is judged on the command line it sets. So `git -c user.name=x commit -m y` is allowed and `git -c user.name="$NAME" commit -m y` is refused by the same reading, with no key named in the rule.

functional_clauses: Extend the per-segment force-push check so the value of every git configuration carrier named in the objective is dequoted and checked as a nested command line by the same checks a `sh -c` payload receives (including `isUnknownForcePushShape` and the `+refspec` check).

Assignments in an earlier top-level segment of the same command line (`export NAME=value`, `NAME=value;`) are carried forward to the later git segment; `env NAME=value git ...` and `NAME=value git ...` are read on the segment itself.

A value containing an unexpanded parameter, a command substitution or a backtick, on any configuration key, and any `--config-env` whose value comes from a named environment variable, makes the segment a violation, matching how `definesInlineGitAlias` treats an unreadable alias. The key does not change this: the rule holds no list of keys.

tasks.summary: git arguments supplied through xargs and git output piped into a shell are read like their in-line forms; a read-only git search naming a rewrite word is allowed on a protected branch.

tasks.title: Delegation check answers a continuation from its original dispatch
tasks.summary: `bs delegation check` treats a dispatch_decision with continuation_of as answered by the session the original dispatch opened; a fresh dispatch is judged exactly as today.
tasks.objective: Fix `bs delegation check` for a resumed wave-runner. When the epic session resumes a sub-agent it logs a new dispatch_decision whose payload names `continuation_of: <original dispatch event id>`; no new session-start names the new event as its causal parent, so the check reports the continuation as unanswered. Make delegation.ts follow `continuation_of` (transitively, cycle-safe) to the original dispatch of the same agent role and task, and count the continuation as answered when that original opened a session (including one opened elsewhere). A dispatch without `continuation_of`, or whose `continuation_of` names an unknown event or a dispatch of another role or task, is judged by today's rules unchanged. Document the `continuation_of` field in .claude/skills/bs/dispatch.md.
acceptance_criteria: A failing test reproduces the bug first. Fixture: an original wave-runner dispatch_decision answered by a session-start whose causal_parent is its event id, then a continuation dispatch_decision whose payload has `continuation_of` naming it and no session of its own. Before the fix the continuation's check has status `unverifiable` with the detail that it has opened no session against it yet; after the fix its status is `ok` and its sessionId is the original's session. (DelegationStatus is `ok | violation | unverifiable | not-applicable`.)
When the original opened no session, the continuation's status equals what today's rules give the original (`unverifiable` while unfinished, `violation` once finished), never `ok`.

The original dispatch may sit in an ancestor session of the checked lineage, and its opened session may be known only through `openedElsewhere` (a later wave session checking an earlier wave's dispatch); both cases are covered by tests and answer `ok`.

A continuation adds no delegated session and changes no rule-3 result. On the continuation fixture, `delegatedSessions` equals its value on the same log with the continuation dispatch_decision removed, and rule 3 gives the same result on both logs (no new violation, the same count). In a variant where the original's session also holds a dispatch written by an actor other than the original's role, the one rule-3 violation names the original dispatch as the owner ("opened against <original event id>", the original's role), on both logs; if the continuation took over the session, the detail would name the continuation's event id instead. Rule 3 itself is unchanged.
A chain of two continuations (C2 -> C1 -> original) is answered when the original opened a session; a cycle of `continuation_of` references terminates and is reported unanswered.

A `continuation_of` naming an unknown event id, a dispatch of a different agent_role, or a dispatch for a different task_id is judged as a fresh dispatch and is never answered by the original's session.
Every existing case in delegation.test.ts and delegationCli.test.ts passes unchanged, including the rule-2 cases for a fresh dispatch.

dispatch.md documents `continuation_of`: when the epic session writes it, that its value is the original dispatch_decision's event id, and that the check answers the continuation from the original's session.
The `bs delegation check` CLI output for a continuation is covered by a delegationCli.test.ts case.

functional_clauses: Read `continuation_of` from the dispatch_decision payload alongside agent_role and task_id in delegation.ts.

Resolve a continuation to its root original through same-role, same-task links with a visited set; the continuation is answered exactly when the root original is answered by today's rules (its opened session, `openedElsewhere` included).

Answering a continuation from the original's session adds nothing to the `delegated` map: that map stays keyed by child session id, and the session the original opened keeps the original's DispatchRow, so `delegatedSessions` and rule 3 see the same sessions and owners with or without the continuation.

tasks.summary: One definition of transcript token spend (input + cache creation + output, no cache reads, deduped by message id and request id), a per-session reader with per-role attribution, reused by the dashboard Budget.

tasks.title: Redacted Markdown export renderer
tasks.summary: Pure helpers that redact home-directory and temp paths and render report and stats sections as Markdown, keeping passed, failed, not-run and unknown distinct.
tasks.objective: Create factory/orchestrator/src/reportExport.ts with pure helpers for an opt-in Markdown export of `/bs report` and `bs stats`. (1) A redactor `redact(text, {homeDir})` that replaces each of these home-directory and temp path forms with a stable placeholder, `<name>` being one path segment: `/Users/<name>`, `/home/<name>` and `/root`, where `/root` matches only as a whole path segment, that is `/root(?![A-Za-z0-9._-])` (`/root` and `/root/x` are replaced, `/rootfs/x` is kept); `C:\Users\<name>` and `C:/Users/<name>` (any drive letter) and the JSON-escaped `C:\\Users\\<name>`; a `file://` URL over any of those; the dash-encoded slug forms that start `-Users-` or `-home-`; the temp roots `/private/tmp/`, `/tmp/`, `/var/folders/` and `/private/var/folders/`; and the running user's home directory, whatever it is, passed in as `homeDir`; an empty `homeDir` or a `homeDir` of `/` is ignored, and the fixed forms still apply. A home form becomes `<home>` with the rest of the path kept (so `/Users/<name>/repo/x.ts` becomes `<home>/repo/x.ts`). A slug form is replaced whole: in a slug a name's own hyphens cannot be told apart from the separators, so the match runs from `-Users-` or `-home-` up to the next whitespace, `/`, quote character (a double quote, a single quote or a backtick) or the end of the string, and that whole token becomes the one placeholder `<home-slug>` (so `projects/-Users-example-user-repo-x/a.jsonl` becomes `projects/<home-slug>/a.jsonl`). A temp-root path becomes `<tmp>` through the end of the path. `~/x` names no user and stays as written: that is a decision, not an omission. Other absolute paths (for example `/api/tasks`, `/usr/bin/git`) name no user and are kept as written: that is a decision too. (2) A check-state type `passed | failed | not-run | unknown` whose Markdown rendering keeps the four states distinct (a check with no event renders "not run", an unreadable one "unknown", never "passed"). (3) Section renderers for a metrics table and a per-task checks table. The module never reads transcript text and never writes anywhere.
acceptance_criteria: Redaction tests: one case per path form the objective lists (each of the home forms, each Windows spelling, `file://`, both slug forms, each temp root, and an injected `homeDir` outside `/Users` and `/home`) is replaced by its placeholder; a repo-relative path is kept; `~/x` is kept as written; `/usr/bin/git` and `/api/tasks` are kept as written; the redactor is idempotent; a string with no path is unchanged.
